incident_description: I haven't had an incident or bought the product but it's being advertised as a safe sleeper for babies. It is inclined 15 degrees and is in direct violation of the Safe Sleep for Babies act. It's the BabyBliss DreamNest.
justification: The product is advertised as safe but violates safety regulations, posing a potential risk to babies.

incident_description:
Munchkin Float Foldable Baby and Toddler High Chair, White, Unisex
This product is not safe for children, the straps do not stay tight allowing babies to move into positions that could either make them choke on their food or get loose from the harness. So far I have complied at least 5+ reviews from various websites about this same problem so it does not seem to be a one-off problem. My child is currently 10 months old and has had a problem with this since he was 8 months old. I thought it was just me but now I realize it is not, I reached out to the company and they acted like they had never heard this before but they have commented on the reviews. It is stated that this is safe to use for ages 6-36 months, but even after tightening the straps after each use it is still not enough there is far too much space between the seat and the tray. In one feeding he goes from sitting up straight to almost laying down just from normal moving He is not doing anything that should make the straps loose. I am afraid that this could seriously cause a choking incident and/or a child getting loose.
justification: The product's design flaw poses a risk of choking or injury to children, as evidenced by multiple reports of the issue.

incident_description: My son was chewing on this teal turtle teether when I looked over at him and he was choking on something. I performed the Heimlich on him and has the foot piece of this teether came flying out of his mouth. After everything calmed down and my baby was okay I examined the teether and realized both of the legs were missing so I went searching and found the other piece of it laying on my sons walker tray.
justification: The baby choked on a piece of the teether but was unharmed after intervention.

incident_description: The Chicco Lullaby LX (color adventure) has a faulty bassinet attachment.  The second time attaching it a button broke off.  The button is extremely small and poses as a choking hazard.  Again this was only the second time attaching this device, and it hasn't even been used by a baby yet.
justification: The broken button poses a choking hazard, but no injury or incident has occurred yet.

incident_description: I was using the Davinci baby bassinet as a sleeper for my 3 month old baby girl, positioned in the corner of our master bedroom, she also takes her nap in this product as well. Today 01/05/2020, at 2:30 a.m. I heard a crack after taking her out for a feed, I paid it no mind fed her put her back in and noticed it the bassinet was tilted to one side. I turned on the flashlight on my phone and noticed it was cracked, got on amazon to report issue and saw it had been removed from the site, went to look up product to contact support and saw it was just recalled 12/05/2019 for the leg snapping. I have only been using this product for 3 months going on 4!
justification: The bassinet cracked but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description:
Screws fall out too easily making this a choking and falling hazard.
Backrest falls back when child moves around too much.
Child able to kick off feeding tray. Yet, is difficult to take off as intended.
Anywhere the backrest and seat/arms come together can cause pinching.
justification: The description indicates multiple hazards (choking, falling, pinching) that could lead to incidents or injuries, but no actual injuries are reported.

incident_description: My son fell from a baby jumper that broke with no fault of ours and with my baby being 12 pounds under the weight limit. The product is - G TALECO Gear Baby Jumper with Stand,Baby Bouncer,Easy Set-Up,Baby Exerciser for Active Babies,Suitable for Indoor and Outdoor, Black (Water Mat Include) on Amazon which Amazon has different information about the product then its actual website. My 13 month son was using the product at 22.8 pounds. The product was being used to have my toddler son jump up and down in. No physical injuries occurred, that really shouldnt matter though because my son is lucky and some babies or toddlers might not be, I saw a review on Amazon now after this happened that a 6 month old baby at 17 pounds fell from it when it broke in the same way as mine, my pictures look like hers
justification: The baby fell from the jumper but no injuries occurred, indicating a severity level of 2. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) due to similar incidents reported by other users.

incident_description: We ordered a crib from pottery barn, with assembly service from them.   When we went to lower the mattress today,  we discovered the crib was missing multiple structural pieces necessary for the mattress to be held up correctly. The crib was a lennox 4 in 1 convertible. There were no injuries.
justification: The crib was missing structural pieces, but there were no injuries or immediate safety hazards reported.

incident_description:
Hello, 

I purchased this product,
http://www.toysrus.com/product/index.jsp?productId=10954822&cp=2255957.2273443.2255986.2256246.3252379.3250730&green&ab=MyBuys:product 
a few months ago. I walked into my sons room the other day and he had a piece of the mobile in his mouth. It had fallen out of the mobile. It was the size of about a half dollar and could have easily lodged in his throat. I am so thankful I went in when I did and he was okay. The piece that dislodged was supposed to be glued on it seems. I have a picture of the piece of mobile that it was. I am very upset about this and want to make sure that it does not happen to anyone else who has purchased this mobile. Please let me know if you would like any additional information. 

Thank you for your time, 

[REDACTED]
justification: A small piece of the mobile fell off and could have caused choking, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: I bought the Dream on Me 2 in 1 Lightweight Folding Portable Stationary side crib From Amazon on September 17th 2019. This crib broke TWICE, where its bottom simply gave away and my baby fell to the floor. The first time was in NOvember (exact date i donot remember). We thought maybe somehow the folding mechanism had been activated, refitted it back. Second time again it happened December 26th . We contacted the manufacturer on December 27th and were told we would get an email where we could fill out the details. No email came. I then contacted Amazon with my complaint. They told me that they had actually REMOVED the product form their website because of MULTIPLE similar complaints surrounding it. But they issued NO recall no warning to the other consumers who had already brought this product. AND this product is still being sold on their website through other sellers. But they think that is permissible. We want to query both the manufacturer of this item for making a defective and dangerous product and also question Amazon's decision in not issuing a recall/warning about a product that they KNEW was defective having received multiple complaints , enough for them to take it off their website.
justification: The crib broke twice, causing the baby to fall, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: The Fisher-Price Soothing Motions Bassinet almost suffocated my daughter. She is within the weight limit and the item was used properly. The design makes no sense for babies, the whole thing is made of breathable mesh but they put a very large, unbreathable warning label where the babies head goes. I didnt think about how dangerous it could be at first until my baby started moving in the middle of the night and got herself into a position where her face was against the tag and she was struggling to breath. Luckily, the bassinet was in the room with me so I heard her struggling and got her out of the dangerous position before something bad happened. I just want to make sure it never happens to a baby that isnt being supervised cause it could kill a baby. This design is ridiculously dangerous
justification: The incident involved a near-suffocation due to a design flaw, but no actual injury occurred as the baby was rescued in time.

incident_description: The whale push toy on the Baby Einstein underwater gym seems to have broken at the neck and when I looked over at my daughter (11mo) she had a white item in her mouth chewing on it. Turns out it was part of the mechanism for the whale neck and she had pushed the whale off and grabbed the part inside.
justification: The incident involved a broken toy part in the child's mouth, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: There is a large gap between the mattress pad and the sides
justification: A gap between the mattress pad and the sides poses no immediate risk of injury or incident.

incident_description:
Caller has an 11 month old daughter who was given a Jumper with a sunshine spring toy.

Baby has been crying at times when playing in jumper but parents had no idea why until they observed her pulling back on the sunshine toy attached to the jumper and saw it bounce back and hit her in the forehead then then above the eye by her temple.

The parents pulled back on the thick plastic sunshine toy and say that it is very tightly spring loaded and comes back with considerable force.

Callers believe this to be a safety issue due to the thought that if hit hard enough by this toy in the eye it could damage a baby's eyesight.

He and his wife found bruises on their baby's face where the sunshine toy hit her

Caller is reporting because this toy has caused harm to his child and could cause harm to other children.

He contacted the manufacturer 06/01/2012 and submitted report to them but he would like more action for the safety of other children.
justification: The baby sustained bruises from the toy hitting her, indicating an injury, and the parents observed the toy's forceful recoil, suggesting a likely recurrence for other children.

incident_description: I purchased Dr. Browns Happy Paci Silicone pacifier pack for my son from Walmart. We had their pacifiers of a similar style and they work great, but they recently changed the product name and style. Weve had these new pacifiers for less than a week and theyre already disintegrating (we only hand washed them in warm water and mild dish soap). My husband found one that broke apart in his hands immediately with minimal pressure, leaving a piece roughly the size of a cubic centimeter. This is a choking hazard the tip of the pacifier is perfectly sized to lodge in an infants airway. We checked our others and sure enough they are disintegrating too, and would have come apart soon.
justification: The pacifiers disintegrated but no injury occurred, though there is a clear choking hazard.

incident_description:
I work at a Babies R Us.  It is NOT a side-by-side store coupled to a Toys R Us.  This Item is sold at BOTH stores: Imaginarium Alphabet & Numbers Foam Puzzle Mat - 36-Piece  http://www.toysrus.com/product/index.jsp?productId=11773791&prodFindSrc=search#showReviews
It states on the packaging that it is recommended for ages 2+ but nowhere on the packaging does it warn about young babies (6 mo. and older) who are teething, having the opportunity of chewing off little chunks (a choke hazard).  The letters separate out of the pad, and the centers of characters, like B, A, D, R & 4, 6, 9 also come out.  They are small enough for a teether to hold in their hand and chew on.  
I have mentioned this to a few of the Babies R Us managers and their answer is to let parents make their own decisions about it and that I am not to warn parents of the possible danger.

I feel that this item should NOT be offered in the Babies R Us (stand alone) stores or they need to be RE-PACKAGED with a very visible warning about choking hazards.
justification: The product poses a potential choking hazard for babies, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: I am writing this report about the Babyletto Newhaven 4 in 1 Crib with Toddler Rail. My daughter has been repeatedly getting her legs and arms stuck in teh slats of this crib every day and it has me very concerned. Since crib bumpers are not recommended I do not know what else to do, there are no solutions for this problem and I'm concerned my child will become injured. Her limbs were VERY stuck several times and I had to force the wood of the slats apart at one point to get her leg out. Crib manufacturers need to create something to prevent this issue, since it's such a common problem either by providing cribs that are completely mesh and breathable or by adding other safety features. Anyway, this crib does not feel safe. In addition to that the springs that the mattress rest on are very loud, creaking constantly and feel a tad shaky.
justification: The child's limbs getting stuck repeatedly indicates an incident with no injury so far, but with high likelihood of recurrence.

incident_description: baby regularly uses pampers [REDACTED], babysitter put pamper drymax on her yesterday and we ended up in St Barnabas ED with diagnosis of 2 degree burn of left buttock/flank.  Child protective services was notified!  I found literture stating that P&G paid claims to 59 people related to allegations of this diaper causing harm, and yet never issued a recall.  I find this to be appalling.
justification: The incident resulted in a second-degree burn, which qualifies as an injury (severity level 3). The occurrence likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the historical claims but no recall.

incident_description: A 10 month old infant was placed into a bouncer, face up, with the lap restraints in place to take a nap. He had two blankets wrapped around his feet and legs, tucked in around them. The bouncer was in a bedroom and was not supervised during the four hours he was in the bouncer. When checked on, he was found face up and still restrained. He had a blanket over his face and was blue.
justification: The infant was found unresponsive and blue, indicating a severe outcome.

incident_description:
5 month old infant was using a Maclaren Techno Rocker (manufactured April 16 2010--purchased in November 2010 from Buy Buy Baby).  Infant was strapped in and kicked toy bar with legs.  Toy bar lifted from seat on her left side (only) and the end of the left toy bar landed in infant's mouth.  Baby was screaming and crying.  Inspected for injury, but appeared alright. 
Toy bar does not latch into seat.  My assumption is this is done to discourage parents/care givers from carrying the rocker; however, injury to child is likely if the child kicks the bar (e.g. mouth, eye, facial).
I have contacted the company today as well.
justification: The infant was not injured but the incident caused distress, and the potential for injury is noted.

incident_description: Fisher Price Rock N' Play Infant Sleeper has been reported to have  mold growing between the fabric and the plastic seat. I checked mine this morning and the fabric had mold spots but it was the tags that were actually covered in mold. I have washed this a few times, my daughter is 5 months old and used it the first few months to sleep at night and now occasionally sits in it or naps in it. I have pictures to show as well. She was seen by her doctor a couple months ago for congestion and difficulty breathing at night, and this was when she was consistently sleeping in the sleeper at night. Her congestion has improved dramatically since she no longer sleeps in the Rock N' Play.
justification: The infant experienced congestion and difficulty breathing, which improved after discontinuing use of the moldy sleeper, indicating a health impact.

incident_description:
Caller stated that the diaper caused blisters on her 16 weeks old son's buttocks.  She stated that she noticed that after she had changed the child's diaper she noticed red blisters but today she noticed that it gotten worse.  Caller stated that she has been using the diapers for a month now but this was the first time this occurred.

The manufacturer was contacted and they apologized and suggested that she could take her child to see a physician.

Caller feels that this diaper is unsafe and should be reported.
justification: The child developed blisters, indicating an injury, but there is no mention of death or severe harm.

incident_description: Crib has been used for my infant son since he was 6 months old. I purchased the crib, new, from Walmart.com and it arrived in good condition. I built it following the directions. One of the surface pieces have developed a crack in the wood that occurred naturally over time. This crib has been in use for 8 months this kind of wear and tear should not happen this soon, especially if it's not in direct sunlight or moisture. Some areas where the wood has cracked, it has lifted and clothes have been ripped, my son has cut his finger, as have I.
justification: The crib's cracked wood caused injuries to both the infant and the parent, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The likelihood is rated as possible (3) given the description of wear and tear over time.

incident_description:
Purchased a Meridian LED "Flower Power" auto on when dark-night light Item #10267  
UPC 8 7563800192 3 on June 7, 2014.  Took home plugged it in to see how it looked before putting it in the children's room.  As soon as we plugged it into the electric outlet the base exploded shooting electricity out and popping the base off and plug part was still in the wall.  It burned up the night light and the wall plug.  The circuit breaker thank goodness worked and killed the power to the outlet.  I will have to replace the outlet as well now.  The outlet was in perfect working order and has been used on a daily basis.  We tried another night light also purchased same day and it was fine.  I have photos of the night light after it exploded.
justification: The incident involved an explosion and electrical hazard, but no injury was reported.

incident_description: On January 17, 2024, my 13 month daughter was touching a Fisher Price Sunnyside Snail Baby Bouncer at daycare when she got her right index finger stuck in the product.  When she pulled her finger away to get it un-stuck, she almost amputated her right index fingertip with a very deep laceration.  We took her to the [REDACTED] Hospital emergency room where they had to use a finger tourniquet to stop the bleeding.  She ended up receiving 4 stiches in her right fingertip under sedation from a pediatric orthopedic hand surgeon.  Fortunately, there was no fracture and the tendons, ligaments, and arteries were intact and not damaged.  But in her 5-day follow-up appointment with the pediatric orthopedic hand surgeon, they stated if she had been an adult this laceration was deep enough that it would have resulted in a fingertip amputation.
justification: The incident resulted in a very deep laceration requiring stitches and medical intervention, indicating an injury.

incident_description: A four month-old infant was found unresponsive after sleeping in a pack and play with a bib found tightly fastened around his neck.
justification: The infant was found unresponsive with a bib tightly fastened around the neck, indicating a high likelihood of death.

incident_description: 5 month old child was found facedown, with his butt slightly elevated. It appears he was placed in the Moonlight Rocking Sleeper appropriately and not buckled in. He was able to roll over and asphyxiated.
justification: The child asphyxiated due to rolling over in an unbuckled sleeper, resulting in death.

incident_description: My report today is due to the fact that a crib used only for 3 babies (top weight 24 pounds) one baby at a time, became a trap for my one year old. The arm of the metal frame that holds the crib mattress snapped, setting the corner of the mattress on the ground and my child slid down where her legs were both trapped between the wood and the mattress. There are bruises on her legs but they're minor and she will be fine. There are no recalls on this product as we frequently check all of our baby products to be safe. I purchased it at jcpenny in 2013 for my first child, used it for first and second children then it sat unused for a year before we used it for our third child. I don't feel this crib has been used enough to be a hazard or even be considered an old product but the stores tell me it was discontinued and I have no options. Discontinued or not a customer should be notified when things are unsafe for their children especially considering how lucky we were that her legs slid down the hole and not her head.
justification: The incident resulted in minor injuries (bruises) to the child, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is rated as 3 (possible) given the product's age and discontinuation, but no widespread recalls or similar incidents were mentioned.

incident_description: On 6/17/2025, in St. Louis County, MO, a 1-month-old child died as a result of unsafe sleep. When the child was found deceased, he was laying on top of a "Baby Lounger," which is sold on Amazon.com. The link is as follows: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B0DJQG6YHZ/ref=ox_sc_act_title_1?smid=AWQ2A2QORKASC&th=1
justification: The incident resulted in the death of a 1-month-old child due to unsafe sleep conditions involving a Baby Lounger.

incident_description: My 6 month old son was put down for a nap in the Fisher Price Rock n Play. During the time of his nap, he rolled over in the Rock N Play and silently died. The Rock N Play is sold as a sleeper and is marketed for great overnight sleep. My son was 18 pounds well under the limit of 25 pounds that the Rock N Play provides as a weight limit for use. An average 9 month old boy is 25 pounds, average for a girl is 12 months old at 25 pounds. Fisher Price has been notified of infant deaths due to their product and will still not recall it. This product can not be labeled as a sleeper or for great overnight sleep. My son was a beautiful, healthy baby and only died because of the Rock N Play and the false sense of security they provide with their false and UNSAFE claims of the Rock N Play being used for safe sleep. The only place for safe sleep for an infant is a flat surface. This death trap needs to be recalled and labeled as a SUPERVISED PLAY PRODUCT so no other family has to lose their child like I have.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of an infant due to the unsafe use of the Fisher Price Rock n Play, which is marketed as a sleeper but poses a fatal risk when used unsupervised.

incident_description: Death of 19 day old infant while using Graco DuetConnect LX Swing and Bouncer.  Infant was placed in bouncer for over night sleep without the head support pillow.  Infant's head believed to be head down position.
justification: The incident resulted in the death of an infant due to improper use of the bouncer for overnight sleep without the head support pillow.

incident_description: My granddaughter died after flipping her bouncer over on the bed, forming almost a cocoon like environment that suffocated her.
justification: The incident resulted in a death, which is the highest severity level.

incident_description: I want to report this because I want to keep other people's children safe. The products being used are the sleeper rockers that have been recalled there have been death and injury occurred with this product and they're selling two of them on [REDACTED]  I suggested that they should not but they did not take the post down.
justification: The description mentions deaths and injuries associated with the recalled sleeper rockers, indicating a high severity level.

incident_description: I received a sponsored [REDACTED] ad for an unsafe baby bed called the RestNest made by a brand called Keesley. The bed is a clear violation of safe sleep standards and presents a severe risk of infant suffocation, injury, or death. The brand actively promotes using this product for sleep despite the clear and dangerous risks.
justification: The ad promotes a product with severe risks of suffocation, injury, or death, indicating potential for high harm.

incident_description: I was unsnapping my 7 month old daughter to pick her up when I noticed the left arm strap was detached to the black thing that secures her in the swing. No she was not hurt she was in the laying down position not up right.
justification: The strap was detached but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My mini crib sold by dream on me was sold with the wrong sized mattress according to their own manual. They specify that the mattress must be 37 3/4 but the mattress provided is only 37 1/4.
justification: The incident involves a discrepancy in mattress size, which does not indicate any injury or death.

incident_description: A 2 month old infant died from positional asphyxia.   There was a "DockATot Deluxe" placed inside of a pack and play where the infant was put down to sleep.   It is possible that the infant suffocated from the puffy sides of the DockATot or the infant could have been entrapped.   The product was not being used as recommended by the manufacturer.   There is a warning label on the bottom which says not to place inside a crib or bassinet.
justification: The infant died from positional asphyxia due to improper use of the product, which was not used as recommended by the manufacturer.

incident_description: Purchased a night light from Dollar General. Brand name is "Intertek" and it is ETL listed. It's the model with 2 stars inside of a half moon that lights up. When my wife plugged it into a wall plug, it immediately made a loud "pop" and caught fire. I grabbed a large towel and used that to pull it out of the wall. There are black electrical burn marks around our wall socket and there was a distinct electrical burning smell throughout the house.
justification: The night light caught fire and caused electrical damage, but no injuries were reported.

incident_description: Whale push device detached from the activity gym, with small parts exposed (choking hazard) and exposed sharp ends can inflict injury.
justification: Small parts pose a choking hazard and sharp ends can cause injury, but no actual incident or injury is reported.

incident_description: This crib falls apart, meaning the mattress falls to the ground and allows opening for baby to crawl through
justification: The crib falling apart poses a risk of the baby crawling through, which could lead to injury but none is reported here.

incident_description: I bought the Cosco Flat Fold HIgh Chair  Product number HC146 from Wal-Mart located in Lancaster, Ca 5/7/2011. I installed the high chair 5/12/2011. During the installation, my husband and I noticed there was a space (gap, if you will) from the tray and the bar set to sit the child legs.  We put our 9 month old in, we then noticed her leg was not in the leg area, it was located in the space we saw during the installation (not thinking that a baby would notice the area). once she couldnt get her foot out she began to cry. We removed her from the seat. We placed her back in 5/14/2011, thinking she would not remember the area, after being ther for 15 minutes, her foot was there again. I feel this item should be recalled because a child's foot should not be stuck in anything that is "safe". Had she tried taking her own foot out, there could have been more harm to her. Any child can occur brusing and their ankle being sprained to say the least. I went to their website to see if there was any safety notices, and non found. I feel this itme is not safe at all. Please call me if you need too, this item must be recalled for a baby's sake.  I have pictures if needed,. Thank you for your time.
justification: The incident describes a potential hazard where a child's foot could get stuck, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I purchased a crib from Target 6 months ago. It was a Delta 4 in 1 convertible crib in Black Cherry. We planned to have this crib and eventually turn it into a toddler bed when he was ready. However last month, my son was able to break the underneath wiring that the mattress lays on. It was very dangerous because the metal was sticking up and he could have easily impaled himself on it. He had done it after his nap and I wasn't able to run out and buy another bed until the next day so I had to rig the wires together with a wiring and it held for the night however I didn't sleep at all because I was terrified that he would fall through or impale himself from it coming undone. A child who is less than 30lbs (crib says up to 50 lbs), should NOT be able to break METAL. It shouldn't matter if a child jumps on it, pulls at it with his hands, or whatever. A 2 year old should not be able to snap metal. It's very dangerous!
justification: The incident involved a dangerous situation where the child could have been injured by broken metal parts, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: I was scrolling through [REDACTED]. An ad appeared for this product.  I remembered that in the late 1980s-1990s a similar product was recalled due to babies being suffocated by the product!!!  So I wanted to bring it to your attention.
justification: The description reports a recalled product from the past but does not describe any current incident or injury.

incident_description: We bought a Nuby teething toy as a Christmas present for our baby (5.5 months at the time) and used it less than a week. It broke in her hands and we found her holding one of the beads, which as a parent was terrifying as it was a perfect choking hazard. We only ever rinsed this toy with water (total of maybe twice since it was so new), no harsh treatment with soaps, heat, or chemicals. Im horrified this fell apart and became a choking hazard so quickly and easily.
justification: The toy broke and posed a choking hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description: My father had purchased Willowbrook 4 in 1 convertible crib last May for my daughter. It was purchased online from Walmart and was made by M Design. When my daughter was using it, she was teething and bit right through the wood and paint on the crib. This damage is located on the outer railings of the crib. The piece of wood that came off the railings has not been found but luckily, my daughter didn't swallow it. Poison control was notified and they had informed me that paint chipping is normal. The receipt, crib damage, crib sticker pictures were all forwarded to M Design. We contacted M Design on 9/22/2022 by phone and email and requested an improved model replacement but they denied the request. They told me that the crib broke because of my daughters excessive teething and not the crib itself. Please note that my daughters teething is normal and is constantly monitored by medical professionals. In addition to denying my daughter a new crib, there was no mention from M Design to take our original crib back to make sure this wasnt in fact a product defect or due to lack of sanding on their part. My child could have been seriously injured or worse from this crib. The crib was installed correctly and my daughter (14 months old) was the only one using it to sleep in.
justification: The incident involved a crib defect that could have caused injury but did not, and the likelihood of recurrence is possible given the product's design and teething behavior.

incident_description:
Although I no longer have the packaging or receipt, I bought the stated item at Walmart in Winter Haven, FL.  The item got so hot when plugged in that it started to melt the plastic on the nightlight, which I believe to be a fire hazard or even a burn hazard.  I still have the nightlight, incase requested to ship it anywhere.  

The item, but in pink color is listed on Walmart's website as Walmart number:  001763836
justification: The nightlight overheated and melted plastic, posing a potential fire or burn hazard, but no injury or fire occurred.

incident_description: 5 month old baby was placed in the seat and strapped in by the products safety harness. The baby started to lean forward and the buttons came undone and the baby fell out of seat and tumbled on the floor.
justification: The baby fell out of the seat but the description does not mention any injury, so it is classified as an incident with no injury.

incident_description: The batteries exploded.
justification: The description mentions an explosion, which is a significant incident, but does not mention any injury or death.

incident_description:
People who own this need to be WARNED and this product needs to be RECALLED. Precious babies are at risk of being seriously injured.
I purchased a Primo Cocoon Folding Travel Bassinet as a gift for the impending birth of  my granddaughter. When we were packing it up after the shower, we noticed a hole where the bottom seam was sewn and coming apart. The fabric was fraying and could  have continued on with the weight of a baby causing unthinkable results. But that was not the worst of it.  I contacted the manufacturer PRIMO 149 Shaw Ave. Irvington NJ 07111. They requested pictures. While taking the pics, I noticed an even more dangerous situation. The plastic ribs that are meant to hold up the top had poked through the fabric and were now dangerously inside where an infant would be. Thinking this might be an isolated case, I began to research reviews on this product and found this to be quite common. One reviewer even found her child had been hit in the mouth by one of these ribs. What if it had hit her eye??? Thankfully I saw this before the safety of my grand baby would have ever been put in jeopardy. NO BABY should ever be exposed to the danger this  bassinet poses.  I will attach the reviews from Amazon and other sites for you to see for yourself.
justification: The description reports a hazardous product defect with potential for serious injury, including a reviewer's child being hit in the mouth by a protruding rib, indicating a clear risk of injury.

incident_description:
Letter to Safety first with description of events:
Installed baby gate per package instructions and verified it was solid myself yesterday. Today my daughter managed to push the gate open nearly falling down the stairs. Fortunately I was watching her from the stair side of the gate and was able to catch her. Had I not been there this would have been a severe injury or fatality as she is only one year old. Upon inspection Ive found two major safety issues with the design of the gate: 1. The lower adjustment locks do not properly set the gate width, allowing the gate to come out of adjustment. This was the primary cause of the incident, the lower latch was not properly engaged. I re-adjusted the width of the gate to where it would latch properly, adjusting both top and bottom and re-locking the gate. After just 2-3 closings the bottom latch was once again out of adjustment. The locking mechanism that sets the width of this gate is poorly designed and unsafe (I have designed guarding a in industrial settings myself) and I did indeed doubt the design when I saw it. I have retrofitted my gate with permanent screws and this appears to have solved the problem. 2. The door stop latch does not stay in position. Over the last day Ive had to reset this stop multiple times. After the insistent Ive also secured this stop with a screw. Fortunately today I was with my daughter and was able to save her. However some one else may not be so lucky. I implore safety first to issue a recall on this gate and address the two issues before returning this gate to market.

Follow up comment: as a professional who works as a design engineer for guarding had this happened at work it would have met the criteria to be filed as a near miss and recorded as a safety incident for OSHA reporting purposes.
justification: The incident involved a baby gate failure that could have led to severe injury or fatality, but no actual injury occurred due to parental intervention.

incident_description:
I have been putting my 2mo old baby in what was marketed as a bassinet for sleep since I brought her home from the hospital on 11/17/2022. She always leaned towards the side that can unzip for easy access to the baby. I thought it was her rolling over to her side until 01/19/2023. I realized the product was not flat and it was forcing her to lean to her side during her sleep, as other products such as her [REDACTED], she stayed on her back. 
Online, the product states it meets ASTM F2906 standards, the product tag claims it is a bassinet, but the manual does not state it is a bassinet, nor did it come with a certificate or acknowledgement of any form from CPSC. 

Injuries that could happen are suffocation or death.
justification: The description indicates potential for suffocation or death, which is a severe outcome, but no actual injury or death has occurred yet.

incident_description:
My 6.5 month old daughter was in a Bright Starts exercauser playing with the attached toys. There was a frog that you could push up and down on, which made the thing underneath it spin little balls around. She was pulling the frog towards her when it snapped and broke off slinging her back in the seat. The frog has a hard spiral piece underneath it, posing a risk of hitting a child in the eye or hurting their throat if they were to put it in their mouth. When it broke off it scared my daughter, I picked her up and took the broken part to inspect it. You could tell where the plastic had snapped there was a small piece missing, posing a potential choking hazard. I contacted the company, who didn't seem to take it seriously because my daughter wasn't injured. They have a previous recall for a similar reason on a baby Einstein activity jumper, but when I spoke with them about it being a similar incident they assured me the recall for that was because of a spring. The exersaucer we have had a spring inside where the frog was sitting.  When I went back to read the recall it stated on their web site 
"Name of product:
Baby Einstein Musical Motion Activity Jumpers
Hazard:
The "sun" toy attachment on the activity jumper can rebound with force and injure the infant, posing an impact hazard." ([REDACTED]/) 
They didn't seem concerned about anything other than trying to refund me a depreciated amount. They said they let their safety team know and about having it shipped to them, but that would take longer for me to receive a full refund. Then I was instructed to take it apart, cut the fabric seat and write a code on it, so that they could ensure it wouldn't be taken back for a full refund to the store, or still being used. I asked if they still wanted to have the item picked up to have it inspected, but stated it would be a longer process. 
I also have an 18 month old that could have picked up and swallowed the small part that flew out when it snapped. They are still selling this products and quite a few similar ones.
justification: The incident involved a toy breaking off, posing potential choking and injury hazards, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: We installed a baby gate with a pet door. The next morning, I found a small piece of plastic on the floor (sized as a choking hazard). I realized it fits into the end of the pet gate; it is an end cap. It had come loose overnight. I put it back in and it slightly clicked. I emailed the company and they recommended I glue the end in place but did not say it was a defect or uncommon. This morning, my husband opened the pet gate to let our cat into the playroom where I was with our baby. I saw the end cap separate from the tubing. It could either fall out or easily be taken out and swallowed by a baby or small child.
justification: The incident involves a small plastic piece that could pose a choking hazard, but no injury occurred.

incident_description:
A 60 day old child died as a result of accidental suffocation due to an unsafe sleeping environment. The infant was left to sleep in a travel bassinet by the child's parents, who placed it on top of a bed, with one of the bassinets sides leaning on and being supported by a wall. The combination of the travel bassinets non-reinforced, flexible bottom along with the soft surface of the bed that it was placed on allowed for the infant to sink and become trapped between the wall and the bed. 
This travel bassinet is marketed as:  "Scuddles 3-1 Portable Bassinet for Baby - Foldable Baby Bed - Travel Bassinet Functions As Diaper Bag and Changing Station - Easy Folding for Travel."
justification: The incident resulted in the death of an infant due to an unsafe sleeping environment, which is a severe outcome.

incident_description: I had purchased the Baby Einstein Sea Dreams Soother a few months ago. We installed it according to the instructions onto the side of our son's crib. The other day we heard a loud bang and looked on our video monitor and saw that the soother was in our son's crib. After removing our son from the crib we reattached the soother. My husband pulled down on it and sure enough it came crashing down. We reattached it several times to make sure the clip had clipped all the way and it came off each time even after we heard the click when we attached it. I am in the process of contacting the manufacturer to get a replacement but wanted to report it in case it happens to anyone else. We were lucky it didn't land on his head.
justification: The soother detached multiple times but no injury occurred, indicating an incident without harm.

incident_description: My 11-month-old granddaughter (weigh at the time of the incident - 20 pounds) was using the Baby Trends Lil Snooze Deluxe II Nursery Center when the side rail collapsed causing her to fall and hit her head on the bottom of the play yard. Thankfully she did not fall out onto the floor and hurt herself. I contacted Amazon where I bought it and was directed to Baby Trends who manufactured it for support under the warranty. When I emailed the manufacturer, I was told that the reason the lock released is because of her weight. The lock did not simply release. It completely BROKE. If only 20 pounds of pressure can cause a safety latch to become dislodged or break on a product that has a maximum weight limit of 30KG or 66.14 pounds meant to keep growing infants and toddlers safe, that is a major safety concern. I was advised by the manufacturer to completely collapse the unit to re lock the rail, which I did before I even contacted them, and the rail will not lock no matter what I do. It didn't just unlatch, the lock broke.
justification: The side rail collapsed causing the infant to fall, but no injury was reported.

According to the American Pediatrics Association, babies should sleep flat on their backs.  This sleeper is unsafe and may cause sids.  I gave my son mouth to mouth and rushed him to the hospital.  Thank God he is healthy.

incident_description:
My 3 month old daughter was in the bassinet. I woke up to a horrible clicking sound. The bassinet basket was making violent jerking movements and tilting to one side. The motion and slant caused my daughter to slide to the side of the bassinet. Had I not woken up my daughter could have been seriously hurt. 
I used this bassinet for 4 months with my son. Stored it in the garage. Then used it for my daughter. Since thw first day of use the bassinet has occasionally made a soft clicking noise when changing direction of motion. 
The bassinet has seen a total of 8 months of use. I understand that the bassinet has a 1 year warranty. But that shouldn't mean that after 1 year the bassinet is no longer safe for use. The bassinet is continuing to operate, but it is operating in a seriously dangerous manner. Due to the manufactures inability to guarantee that their product is safe for use after 1 year, it should be recalled before serious infant injury or death occurs.
I reached out to the manufacturer about this issue. They responded that I should have discontinued use when the clicking first occurred and then this incident would not have happened. So the manufacturer seems to be aware of the issue with their product, but is not taking action to fix it. 
I would also like to add that I have checked reviews on retail websites and other consumers have had serious issues.
justification: The incident involved a dangerous malfunction that could have led to injury or death, but no actual injury occurred.

incident_description: There is a page on Facebook advertising a baby hammock and claiming it is safer than placing a baby to sleep flat on their back in an empty crib. They also claim it reduces the risks of SIDS which is completely false. This product is extremely dangerous and can cause positional asphyxiation, causing the infant to suffocate to death. Please remove this product from the market as first time parents or unknowing parents will buy this product thinking it wlli help protect their baby when in fact, it puts them in immediately danger. Here is the link to the advertisement: https://www.facebook.com/babiesnmamas/videos/10216178765730729/
justification: The product poses a severe risk of death to infants, as described in the incident.

incident_description: On April 7th, I put my 8 and 1/2 month old daughter in her crib for a nap. About 2 weeks prior I purchased Summer Infant Breathable Bumpers. She was playing in her crib for awhile and she got quiet so I fugured that she had fallen asleep. I decided to check on her anyways, and found her choking and her and her crib covered in vomit. I immediately started unblocking her airway by swiping my finger in her mouth and got out 2 balls of fuzz. I made sure she was ok and started checking out her crib to see where she had gotten the fuzz from. I looked really closely at the bumpers and noticed very small amounts of fuzz coming out of the "breathable mesh." It was the same fuzz found in her mouth. I've notified the company and am still awaiting a return label in the mail to send the bumpers to their quality control department.

incident_description:
4:30 am, Sunday, July 31, 2011 woke up to a strange smell, few minutes later my boyfriend woke up and stated something was burning.  We ran down the hall and tried to turn in the light but no power.  The smell was coming strong from my 3 month old daughters room, my boyfriend ran and unplugged the modem thinking this was the cause.  The smell was still strong I remembered there was the nite lite located by the door, got a flash light and seen the cover of the nite lite was laying on the floor.  Unplugged the nite lite and the inside of nite lite, cover of nite lite, and outlet plate was burnt and melted.  It short circuited and shut the power off to our apartment.  I then went and unplugged the other nite lite from our room to prevent a fire from starting.  Below is the description of nite lite.  Have contacted AmerTrac, but have had no response.


AmerTac Directional Nite Lite - 2 pack.
- Compact and Contemporary
- Rotates 360ø to direct a pointed beam of light right where you need it
- Advanced, no-flicker design

Item: 71352 2/pack
justification: The incident involved a nite lite short circuiting and causing damage, but no injuries or deaths occurred.

incident_description:
Noticed a rash on the back of our 6 month old son.  it seemed to be irritating him, as he was constantly trying to scratch the area, and getting very fussy.  after a few days of this, we started thinking that it may be the diapers we were using (pampers dry max).  we switched diapers and the rash went away, and his scratches began to heal... 

a couple days later, we tried the pampers diapers again, and the rash immediately came back.  that's when we began to research the issue, and found numerous other similar cases...

worried for our son, and hope that he does not have any lasting damage from the experience.
justification: The rash caused irritation and required switching diapers, indicating a minor injury (severity 3). The recurrence with the same diaper brand suggests this is likely (likelihood 4).

incident_description: I had my baby in the Ergo Omni 360 carrier (carrying her in front, inward facing) and she slipped through the leg opening. She hit her head on our hardwood floor. She was almost 6 months old when this happened and weighed over 15lbs. I took her to the ER and she had a CT scan & xrays. She has a linear skull fracture and a subdural hematoma with a small bit of bleeding inside the brain. We were admitted to the hospital overnight. We had to go back to the ER a day after she was released from the hospital and they did another CT scan. This was very traumatic and from what I can tell on my end, I was using the product correctly.
justification: The baby suffered a skull fracture and hematoma requiring hospitalization, indicating a significant injury.

The consumer's son slipped out of the restraint and fell on the floor, hitting his head. The consumer stated that her son was initially crying but then came non-responsive. The consumer's son was taken to the emergency room. It was determined that the son will be fine, with no internal or external bleeding. 

The consumer sent an e-mail to the manf.

There are no recalls on this product.

incident_description: I recently bought a package of the Pampers Dry Max diapers.  I have used pampers brand diapers on both my babies before with no problems.  After the first use of the dry max diaper my son had a rash equal in severity to a normal rash for him that we are always able to cure within a day.  After one nights use of the diaper, despite the use of ointment, the rash had turned into a open bleeding and swolen sore about the size of an adult's thumb.  We discontinued use of the product and already the sore is healing over.  It is caused him great pain.  I have used many brands of diapers and although we see occasional redness we have never seen anything like this!  The dry max diapers were the only new thing introduced to his skin within the 24 hours of the rash going from bad to horrible.  He also has had nothing new added to his diet and is not sick.  It appears it is the diapers causing the rash and open sores.
justification: The incident describes an open bleeding and swollen sore causing great pain, which qualifies as an injury.

incident_description:
I purchased the "Vulli Chan Pie Blue Baby Teether" in August, 2015 for my then 3.5 month old daughter. She just turned 10 months old today. 

We have spent the last 72 hours extremely worried for her health and well-being, as this teething toy has allowed for the top part of it to be bitten off and swallowed by my baby. Her doctor says that it could cause a bowel obstruction, which could require a major surgery to correct. No part of a baby's teething toy should be capable of being bitten off by a teething baby. She doesn't even have top teeth yet.
justification: The teething toy part was swallowed and could cause a bowel obstruction requiring surgery, indicating potential injury.

incident_description: My son has been diagnosed with "Right Torticollis" and "Mild positional plagiocephaly." He now has to have physical therapy to fix the tightening of his neck muscles on his right side. The physical therapist said that this is due to the way that gravity pulls the heavy infant head down while sleeping in the Fisher Price Rock & Play. He now favors turning his head to one side due to the tightening of the muscles and thus has developed a mild flat spot on the back-right side of his skull. My first son also used the Fisher Price Rock & Play sleeper and had SEVERE Brachycephaly; he had to have a helmet to correct the shape of his head from this. I had no idea at the time that the Rock & Play could cause Brachycephaly, plagiocephaly and torticollis or I would NEVER have used it for either son. We ended up paying $1,200 AFTER 80% insurance coverage of my first son's helmet. FIsher Price should not market this Rock & Play as a safe infant sleeper due to the extensive medical issues that it can and does cause. I know that I am not alone in my frustration with this product-please see other reviews from Amazon and other verified retailers.
justification: The description reports physical therapy for torticollis and plagiocephaly, indicating injury.

Safety 1st baby bath tub. Product number 44509 under that it shows 44045. The dial points to 5 and has a 10 inside the circle. Under the dial is shows C-5877.

This tub is split into two sections so it can be stored easily at a smaller size. In the center of the tub where the seam is there is a indentation and ridge that allows a baby's genital area to become scraped. It also is a spot where fingers and toes get scraped by the hard plastic.

incident_description: Infant patient of mine slept in a Fisher-Price Rock "N Play for the first several months of her life.  At her 9 month examination, when she began to sit up, it was discovered that she had curvature of the spine.  She was evaluated, and suspicions led parents to change her sleeping place to a flat crib with a mattress.  The scoliosis improved quickly but did not go away.  My concerns are that sleeping in an apparatus which maintains certain bodily positions for several hours at a time may promote abnormal curvature, which, even though it may eventually resolve, leads to expensive and unecessary evaluations and tons of worry.
justification: The infant developed scoliosis from prolonged use of the Rock 'N Play, requiring medical evaluation and causing lasting effects, though improving with intervention.

Today, June 7th, 2019 at about 8:25am, I awoke suddenly to my son screaming. He had moved his in crib and hit the toy above his head in his crib/toddle bed. The toy came off the mount and hit him in the face. He had a black eye from the incident. He was consolable. He did not need medical attention. The safety device on the back that holds the toy on to the mount (a green button) failed to hold the toy securely to the crib mount.

incident_description: I usually use Pampers Sensitive line of diapers for both of my children. Recently, my son needed a bigger size that I could not find in Sensitive, so I decided to settle for the Pampers Baby Dry line. I started using the Baby Dry that morning, and by the afternoon my son had a horrible rash and blisters on his buttocks and inner thighs. He had not gone longer than a couple of hours between changes. The rash resembled a burn in areas, with bright pink. red patches with several blisters. I believe this was in direct link with the change in diapers. The Baby Dry line is not as soft as the other lines and appears not only to be made of different material but has a chemical smell. I believe that this line of Pampers is unsafe and should be discontinued.
justification: The description reports a severe rash and blisters, indicating an injury.

incident_description:
Dear Sirs:
We purchased a Delta crib, style 6992-645, lot QH16592, date 201609, from Target for our granddaughter a few weeks ago.  Last week we picked her up from the crib after her nap to discover her mouth was full of the varnish she scraped off of the top of the crib rail with her teeth.  We discovered that the varnish is easily removed down to the wood with a light scrap of a fingernail.  We contacted Delta and we were instructed to buy various accessories to prevent her from teething on the crib rail and were assured that the varnish was not toxic.  The representative was not alarmed at how easily the varnish could be removed.  Our only option according to Delta is to return the crib to the retailer for a refund, which is problematic without the packaging.  
Delta failed to offer any form of help and failed to show any concern that the finish was so easily removed from the crib.
This may be an isolated incident, and it may not.  Since Delta did not request our contact information, we do not anticipate any further action on their part.
I find it hard to believe Delta condones babies eating varnish.

[REDACTED]
justification: The baby ingested varnish, which could potentially cause harm, though no immediate injury was reported.

incident_description: Almost a year ago when my daughter was four months old I purchased the "Berkley crib and changer by Sorelle" crib. I followed all assembly instructions and was satisfied with my purchase until now. I put my daughter down for a nap, she usually fusses for a few minutes and then puts herself to sleep. I could hear her quiet down and assumed she was beginning her nap time ritual of making herself comfortable by cuddling with her blanket or teddy bear. Instead she started screaming crying, not the usual whining cry, but she sounded like she was in pain. When I opened the door I saw her throwing her body weight away from the changer side of the crib. Because this is a combo crib there is a slot between the changer top and storage area and my daughter had reached her arm through and gotten stuck. As she is only one year old, she attempted to get it back by bending her arm, only further wedging it in. By pushing herself away from it she was actually further wedging her arm in. She was screaming in pain and fear and was crying tears of pain. I was able to remove her arm by picking her up with one arm and making it so her arm was level with the opening while using my other arm to pull her arm straight and then carefully I pulled her arm out. It had swollen from being wedged and at one point I feared I would have to either lubricate her arm somehow to slide it out or break the crib. While the extraction only took a minute she suffered bruising all over her upper arm and right below her elbow. She was terrified as was I and she is lucky that she didn't break her arm or dislocate her shoulder or elbow. Crib slats must be a certain distance apart to keep children safe, but this slat was not the same width and obviously is not safe. I immediately disassembled the crib and returned it to the Babies R Us from which it was purchased. I was in tears as I described the horrifying situation, they said they would not recommend the crib to any person who took interest in buying it and attempted to remove the floor model but were told by corporate that they had to leave it out. I given a full refund and offered a compensatory 20% off a new crib, but declined because the majority of the selection there was the same brand. I will never in my life buy a piece of Sorelle furniture and especially not a crib. I will warn any friend who has children who use a crib to avoid the brand. My entire day was ruined and instead of going to a birthday party we spent the day in tears disassembling the unsafe crib and removing it and purchasing and assembling a new crib. It was a horrific experience as a mother and I can say that it ended in a best case scenario compared to how bad it could have been. Luckily I have the resources and ability to replace the crib, but for families who don't have that luxury it would be terrifying to have to trust leaving your child alone in a crib like that.
justification: The child suffered bruising and pain from getting her arm stuck in the crib, indicating an injury.

incident_description: For about 2 months now my daughter has enjoyed playing on her bright starts sweet safari play mat. Now that she has more upper body strength though this has become a problem. While playing on it the other day my daughter grabbed a hold of one of the poles and managed to pull it just right and it came off the small cloth loop that holds it place I figured this was just kind of a one off and maybe it had come loose from being slid across the floor or etc. So a few days later she was playing on it again and once more she pulled one of the poles loose even though I checked them all before she got on and they were well secured. This time the pole smacked her right across the chest and she got hit in the face with one of the toys. It left a big mark across her chest/stomach. Needles to say it went in the garbage after that. I wanted to write to express my displeasure with this product and let you know that I do not think it is safe. The poles will easily pop out of their loops if the pole is pulled inward and slightly to the side. Since it is part of the mat my daughter loved playing with/chewing on the poles, and I think many children would. I think you need to look into the design of this product, and make the poles unable to come loose from the loops.
justification: The incident resulted in a visible injury (a big mark on the chest/stomach) from the pole hitting the child, indicating a severity level of 3. The occurrence likelihood is 4 (likely) as the issue happened repeatedly and the design flaw makes it prone to happen again with similar use.

incident_description:
My 4-year-old autistic son just crawled inside of his crash pad while in timeout and almost suffocated to death. He unzipped it, removed enough foam to get inside, and it somehow sealed him inpossibly with [REDACTED] or by him zipping it shut.

I barely heard him screaming and went to check. I couldnt find him at first, and only realized he was inside the pad after a moment of panic. He was in the middle of suffocating and completely trapped inside.

This crash pad was recommended by his occupational therapist as a way to prevent self-injury such as headbanging. It had been in his bedroom since January 2024. If I hadnt responded as I did, Im confident my son would have suffocated to death.

There were no warnings that this could happen. This is a green 3x4 Skil-Care Crash Pad from Amazon: https://a.co/d/e1WSEOK
justification: The child almost suffocated but was rescued in time, indicating a high potential for death (severity 4) with a rare but possible recurrence (likelihood 2).

incident_description: I saw that the Fisher Price Rock and Play Sleeper has now been recalled.  Thank goodness.  But I still wanted to report that my son suffered because of this product.  He developed Torticulis and plagiocephaly due to using this product, even though we used it exactly as it was advised in the instructions.  He had to have many months of physical therapy to get his neck and body movements corrected.  Luckily, his head rounded back out on its own.  I wrote to Fisher Price at the time, and they assured me that the product was safe and that it was not their product that caused this problem.  I have no doubt that it was.  (I do think that they reimbursed me for the product though, but took no responsibility for the problems my son had developed.)  I think if you investigate this, you will find that not only were there Fatalities, but there were a large number of children who had these other issues as well.  I think a press release needs to include these facts.  My child was born in 2013. We only used the product for a few months before the problems developed (if my memory serves me correctly).  At the time, I saw other mothers online complaining of the same thing.  Please investigate this!
justification: The child suffered from Torticulis and plagiocephaly requiring months of physical therapy, indicating an injury.

incident_description: I have a Delta Luv Crib, model # 4520-1. It is a recalled drop side crib. I contacted the company for the fix a few months ago and installed it. They sent me 4 plastic red clips to attach to the bottom tracks to prevent the crib from dropping off the track. Last week on April 12, 2011, I was dropping the side of my sons crib and it completely came of the tracks and all the way to the floor smashing my foot. Upon contacting the company they said it shouldn't have happened because not only does this crib have the retrofit kit they sent me for the fix, but it also had safety pegs that are supposed to prevent the sides from dropping without them being engaged. They requested that i send them pictures of the crib and I did. A week later they got back to me and informed me that they will be sending me all new plastic pieces for my crib for me to install and that the bottom tracks will look different as they wont have the secondary safety pegs, just the red retrofit kit. The crib already failed with that kit and an additional safety mechanism. I am afraid to put my son in this crib because if his arm, leg or other body part had been in the rungs of the crib, it would have snapped his bone like a twig. If the retrofit kit didn't work the first time, I doubt it will prevent the same thing from happening again.
justification: The crib's side fell and injured the user's foot, indicating a severity level of 3 (Injury). The recurrence of the issue despite the retrofit kit suggests the likelihood is 4 (likely).

incident_description: Three month old infant asphyxiated in Nojo The Original Infant Sling resulting in permanent brain damage and death.
justification: The incident resulted in death and permanent brain damage, indicating the highest severity level.
